To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

caregivers of children in Kenya believe that diarrhea is a dangerous condition, and that they are reluctant to use oral rehydration salts because of a preference for drugs and confusion about when to use oral rehydraton salts.

(1) diarrhea is perceived to be a dangerous condition; (2) ORT is perceived as less effective than Western medicines for stopping diarrhea; (3) ORT is considered to be a medical treatment requiring prescription and/or supervision; and (4) ORT is not considered to be a first-line treatment for diarrhea.
Caregivers in Kenya believe that diarrhea can be fatal, and that Western drugs are more effective than oral rehydration solution for stopping diarrhea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to improve the quality of ORT in the community.
the need to understand the social and cultural factors that influence the use of ORT and to develop strategies to increase ORT use in the context of a changing health care environment in Kenya.
the role of the health care worker as a key source of information for caregivers and their use of oral re hydration salts and other oral hydration therapy in Kenya.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there was an increase in the use of ORS, which was a result of the increased availability of ORS, the promotion of ORS by the Ministry of Health, and the training of health workers in the use of the ORS packet.
ORT is an effective treatment for diarrhea and should be used in all cases of acute watery diarrhea.
ORT is not used in Kenya because of the belief that Western drugs are better and because ORS is not readily available in rural communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ORS is not a simple task, especially in the rural area.
there is a need for health workers to communicate more clearly about when ORT and ORS is appropriate.
ORT has been underused in Kenya and that the reasons for this are complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of oral solutions to treat diarrhea is still not well understood by many caregivers, even though the solutions have been available for many decades.
health communication should be used to clarify the function and use of ORT in the treatment of diarrhea and to promote ORT as a safe and effective treatment for diarrhea.
ORT is perceived as a treatment rather than a preventive intervention, which has implications for the design of ORT promotion programs.
